open_points.subject: A02
open_points.text: A present value is refused when it is outside the form State 1 declares, at stage (4) of A04 rule 6, every such value named: an alias longer than 40 characters, counted as Unicode code points (R0-90, M01) — its length only, its content being the owner's rule (R0-82); an object kind outside `apartment`, `house`, `commercial`, `other` (M02); a floor area not greater than zero, a number of rooms below 1, or a floor that is not a whole number (M02); a customer language outside `es`, `ru`, `en` (M04).
open_points.question: Is a present Customer kind outside the State 1 vocabulary `person`, `company` refused at stage (4), including when supplied in the import mapping?
options: Accept any nonblank Customer kind because rule 4's exhaustive list omits this check.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a Customer kind outside `person` and `company`, add that condition to rule 4, and require a test for it.

witness.initial: An uploaded import has one picked project whose distinct v1 customer value will create a Customer; the file and all other mapping values are valid.
events: The owner gives the new Customer a valid name and gives `nonprofit` as its kind.
The owner asks for the confirmation step and then confirms if it is shown.
outcomes: Registry refuses the invalid kind and does not show or accept confirmation.
Registry treats the nonblank kind as valid, shows confirmation, and creates a Customer whose kind is `nonprofit`.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether confirmation is available and whether the import is accepted.

open_points.subject: A15
open_points.text: Two accepted changes in turn write entries numbered n and n + 1, and the audit sequence (M12) holds n + 1 after the second; two concurrent changes take two distinct consecutive numbers.
open_points.question: Must the concurrent test establish which change Registry applied first and assert that this change received the lower number, rather than checking only that the two numbers are distinct and consecutive?
options: Control or observe application order and assert that the first-applied change has the lower sequence.
Check only that the two concurrent changes receive the unordered set of two consecutive numbers.
open_points.default_guess: Control the serialization order and assert both consecutiveness and that the first-applied change received the lower number.

witness.initial: The audit sequence is n - 1 and two distinguishable changes A and B are ready to run concurrently.
events: The test arranges or observes that Registry applies A before B.
The test reads the two audit entries and M12 after both changes finish.
outcomes: A has n, B has n + 1, and M12 has n + 1.
B has n, A has n + 1, and M12 has n + 1; a test checking only distinct consecutive numbers still passes.
witness.observer: The test runner and the owner reading the audit log see which action received each sequence.

open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text: The step reads the clock once, before it looks at any file, and compares that UTC instant less 720 hours with each record's UTC instant (L16) at the precision the record holds it.
open_points.question: What precision does a backup record hold, and exactly how is the cutoff compared when the clock reading has finer precision: truncate or round the cutoff to the record's precision, compare the full cutoff with the represented record value, or use another defined rule?
options: Store instants at a fixed declared precision and reduce the cutoff to that precision before the strict comparison.
Treat the record's represented instant as exact and compare it directly with the full-precision cutoff.
Interpret a reduced-precision record as an interval and define retention by one of its bounds.
open_points.default_guess: Declare one UTC instant precision for backup records, truncate the cutoff to that precision, and delete only when the recorded instant is strictly earlier than the resulting cutoff.

witness.initial: The third step reads 2026-11-11T12:00:00.900Z, while a kept backup record stores instants only to whole seconds and contains 2026-10-12T12:00:00Z.
events: The run computes the cutoff by subtracting 720 hours.
Registry compares the cutoff with the backup record.
outcomes: After truncating the cutoff to the record's precision, the instants are equal and the backup is kept.
Comparing the full cutoff with the stored instant makes the backup 0.9 seconds too old, so it is deleted.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the kept backup remains after the run.
